doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Cooking, health food and watercolor painting
summary: Allison cooked and cleaned while Audre taught, made buttermilk cornbread, and painted watercolors.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I don’t have a good enough memory to have copped! But one other thing. Audre was saying earlier that when she was working, you used to make dinner and clean up every night.
Oh, yeah!
So apart from doing all those things artistically, it seems that your humanity is part of the equation as well.
Well, I used to cook when she was teaching school. I cooked every day and I cleaned up.
I used to think, “that’s what it is to have a wife; it’s wonderful—to come home and smell dinner cooking.” It was really nice.
She said you made a mean cornbread.
Oh, yeah. I used to...
You’d cook that up in no-time.
For a while, he was doing that with every meal. It was good.
Instead of rising cornmeal, it...
Buttermilk?
Buttermilk, yeah.
It’s the main ingredient. That’s the main thing.
It’s really delicious. Real crisp on the outside and...
She also said that you cooked a very healthy cuisine.
Remember, we were trying to think of the original woman who wrote the books about healthy...
Adele...
Adele Davis maybe.
Adele Davis! Remember, you read her first book.
I remember your making brown rice with vegetables and...
Getting amino acids without meat, to have cheese and beans... Anyway, he had that cookbook, and then he had something about a natural... You had about three cookbooks that were all...
Diet For A Small Planet.
Yeah. It’s really good. One other thing that he really did well was paint. He did a lot of watercolors.
Oh, we have some really nice watercolors in Mississippi.

When we were first married and we had Alyssa, we were in Jackson, I didn’t have anything to do, and I thought, “Well, I’m a pretty good painter,” and so I got watercolors and paper and all that, and then one day when I wasn’t there, he went out and painted all over Jackson, and I was dumbfounded.
They’re really good. Didn’t you do sort of cartoon stuff when you were young?
No, I didn’t...
Well, that’s what they told me. That’s what Max...
Yes. He’s lying. When your mother played cards...
You used to draw and do caricatures and stuff.
You’d do caricatures of the people at the card table.
He’s a good artist, too.
Anyway, he was a really good painter. He painted the Pearl(?) River(?) (30:52).
I used to draw them.
Oh, you did?
Yeah.
As the characters, yes. But that was the first time you ever tried watercolor.
No. It wasn’t watercolor.
Yes. My watercolors I’m talking about.
He’s talking about when he was young. You’re talking about later.
I’m talking about when you took my...
Later.
Then all his friends said, “Wow” and I thought, “nobody says anything about mine,” so I quit.
